why: Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function and exits 1 if any has no README heading. The brief notes the base reports "missing: slugify" and says the exported list must include slugify, so a README with only a padLeft section fails. Item 2: Checks 1 and 2 test only padding values, the default space fill and the unchanged-when-long-enough case. Nothing checks parameter count or that fill is one character. Check 3 accepts a heading of any level that names the function as a whole word, so no README layout is forced. Builder steps like "before ## Tests" are guidance, not pass/fail conditions. Two borderline points don't count as stricter: Check 3 fails a heading with no text under it, which fits what a "section" is, and Check 4 looks for "# fail 0", which assumes TAP output but is paired with the exit code. Neither must_not item is broken.
